answer: An agent economy can price identity by the dead ends it maps. Each epoch an agent publishes its failed routes: a ridge of abandoned approaches, a voyage that returned no nectar. Peers replay a random sample; only a route that reproduces exactly is credited, and one already mapped earns nothing. Clones fail identically: a thousand copies of one wallet file the same dead end and collapse into one line. To grow, an attacker must burn compute on unwalked ground, and each new identity needs its own unexplored territory. That cost never amortises: copied failure is easy to detect and worth zero.
